one_line: The diff check is cheap (about 0.2 s a run), needs no hook, and sees every committed edit however it was made. With rare, hand-picked identifiers matched on -U0 changed lines it does reach function grain on shared files: in history, 3 of the 13 PRs that touched AppContext.jsx would have fired. As written it breaks in five places: (1) any edit to a whole-file precondition fires (JobDetail.jsx, 11 of 154 PRs); (2) nothing limits common identifiers (useState is in 31% of PRs); (3) it prints only one card, so a do-not-apply warning can be hidden behind another; (4) working-tree runs cannot see untracked files; (5) the `ks close` range picks up other PRs whenever a branch was behind main.

attacks.attack: 1. Whole-file blobs before KS-6b against the hunk-level rule: what does a hunk-level match mean, and what can the KS-5 pilot measure?
attacks.evidence:
Design:284 says `symbol_span` is not built before KS-6b, so the 'changed span' clause is empty until then. Two other clauses turn path overlap back into a warning.
(a) Design:301 sends `--diff`'s changed paths into the exact `ident` lookup, and design:260 lists files as `ident` handles, naming AppContext.jsx as one. A changed path is therefore an exact ident hit, which contradicts §7.1:431's rule that path-only overlaps are not printed.
(b) ex3's precondition is the whole-file blob of JobDetail.jsx (KS-O4, design:283). So 'a changed precondition item' means any edit to that file. In my replay of all 154 first-parent commits on main, ex3 fired through that precondition on 11 PRs, for example 2820fe9 (web-travel-map), cc857d3 (p3e-web-route-closing) and d683faa (jobs-lifecycle-ui), with no ex3 token in their hunks.
What is actually left before KS-6b: plain word tokens from the raw changed lines (comments and strings included, since KS-O1 builds no lexer) intersected with the ident handles; a JSON-pointer value comparison for config items (12 PRs fired on the ex7/ex8 pointers, which is precise); and whole-file preconditions.
attacks.consequence: State the pre-KS-6b rule exactly in §7.1 and §3.7: word tokens from the + and − lines of a -U0 diff, matched against symbol, env-name and error-code idents; config-key value change; no span clause. File-kind idents and whole-file preconditions or protective-test blobs count as path_only (logged, not printed), or the doc says they fire and gives the measured rate. KS-5 can then measure token-rule recall on synthetic diffs, its historical false-fire rate and the config clause. It cannot measure span grain, so the claim of function grain belongs to KS-6b.

attacks.attack: 2. ex3's two pilot requirements: an unrelated edit to another AppContext.jsx function must stay silent, and the naive PaymentModal useState fix must fire. Can the rule as written meet both, and with which ident handles?
attacks.evidence:
PaymentModal is not a separate file. It is a function at JobDetail.jsx:866, used at :675-682. A naive fix that actually works has to touch both files, because logPayment (AppContext.jsx:312-328) must stop minting its own id; the KS-C11 refuters found the same.
I built the variants in a scratch repo from the HEAD blobs (ex3variants.mjs):
- Naive fix, -U0 changed-line tokens: async jobId amount method clientId const useState crypto randomUUID onSave val. Neither logPayment nor PaymentModal is among them.
- With handles {logPayment, logPaymentApi, PaymentModal, randomUUID, clientId, client_id}, the naive fix hits [randomUUID, clientId].
- Unrelated edits (the voidRevenueEntry toast, its comment, the setNegotiatedBill toast) hit nothing under -U0.
- Under -U3 the voidRevenueEntry comment edit fires on logPayment, because the context line AppContext.jsx:332 reads '// logPayment afterward.'.
- Handles taken mechanically from the fix diff fire every unrelated variant (amount, jobId, const).
- An unrelated NegotiateModal edit in JobDetail.jsx fires through the whole-file precondition.
The history replay (appctx.mjs) reproduces the design's figure. Of 13 PRs touching AppContext.jsx, 3 fire with {logPayment, logPaymentApi, PaymentModal} and 10 once useState, payload, onSave, randomUUID, clientId and client_id are added. 11 PRs touched JobDetail.jsx.
Answer: yes, both requirements can be met, but only with -U0, + and − lines, and curated handles that include randomUUID and clientId. The naive fix fires only through those two tokens (each in 8% of PRs) or through the JobDetail.jsx precondition, never through logPayment.
attacks.consequence: Make the KS-2 done-when and §12.7's 'one interpretation' paragraph explicit: -U0, both line signs, curated handles. Record that the naive fix fires through randomUUID/clientId or the JobDetail.jsx precondition. 'Silent on unrelated edits to shared files' does not hold for JobDetail.jsx while its precondition is a whole-file blob.

attacks.attack: 3. Ident handles that are common words or rare in no useful sense (useState, client_id, payload, job, id). What bounds the false-fire rate when matching is exact and not IDF-weighted?
attacks.evidence:
Share of the 154 first-parent PRs whose -U0 changed code lines contain the token (df.mjs):
- useState 47 (31%)
- client_id 34 (22%)
- payload 26 (17%)
- job 89 (58%)
- id 101 (66%)
- method 38, jobId 25, randomUUID 12, clientId 12
- logPayment 10, verify_pin 3, compare_secret 1
Stripping strings and comments barely changes these counts.
Full replay with a realistic 15-entry seed (replay.mjs): under the rule as written, 103 of 154 PRs print at least one warning, against 85 for a path-only join. With high-specificity handles only (replay-strict2.mjs) it is 44, or 27 without whole-file preconditions.
Nothing in the text sets a bound. Ident hits 'are exact handles and do not enter coverage' (§4.1 step 4, K13). §7.3's negative-corpus precision check covers handles firing on known-good HEAD or on unrelated historic failures (symptoms), not diffs.
attacks.consequence: Add a write-gate rule in §7.3 and §3.3: every ident handle that `--diff` uses for a do_not_apply, open_defect or trap entry is replayed against the -U0 changed lines of origin/main's first-parent history and refused or tightened above a set share of PRs (for example 5%). `ks record` prints each handle's historic fire count. For a do_not_apply entry, handles are owner- or author-named guarded identifiers, never derived from the fix diff.

attacks.attack: 4. Edits made through Bash, PowerShell or subagents: does the diff see them, and what does it not see?
attacks.consequence: State in §7.1 that − lines count; that renames are matched with --no-renames, or a rename of a protected file is printed; and §5.5's list of what the diff cannot see (ignored files, out-of-repo state, binaries). 'Needs no hook' stands.

attacks.attack: 5. Working-tree target: KS-F19 uses `git stash create`, which cannot see untracked files, and a new file is exactly the second-door case. Which runs are blind?
attacks.evidence:
In the scratch repo I added a new untracked file that calls verify_pin:
- `git diff <base> --name-only` printed nothing;
- `git diff <base>...HEAD` printed nothing;
- `git stash create` returned an empty string, so there is no snapshot at all when the only change is an untracked file.
KS-F19's guard ('untracked path matches a probe's or footprint's path set') can never fire for a new path. After the file is committed, `git diff <base>...HEAD -U0` shows every line as added.
Blind: the working-tree form of `--diff`, and `ks verify --target worktree` or proposed with a working tree. Not blind: the committed first-commit run, PR-ready, the reviewer at the head SHA, and `ks close`. Even those catch the file only if verify_pin is among ex6's ident handles.
A fix exists. A temporary index outside the repo (GIT_INDEX_FILE, then `read-tree HEAD` and `add -N`) made the untracked file visible to `git diff <base>`. The object count stayed at 23 before and after, and the real index was untouched.
attacks.consequence: Amend KS-F19, §4.1 step 5 and §7.1. Working-tree runs include untracked, non-ignored files through the temporary-index intent-to-add snapshot, or return inconclusive(untracked_present) whenever any such file exists. Never fall back silently to HEAD when `stash create` returns nothing.

attacks.attack: 6. Squash merges and release/drain cherry-picks moving the merge-base: what does <merge-base> mean, and can the diff be empty or cover the whole history?
attacks.evidence:
(a) `ks close` over 'merge-base to the squash commit' (design:344). In 59 of 133 merge-commit PRs on main, the branch was behind main when it merged. For example, ef8ae86's own diff is 1 file with 1 insertion, but the merge-base range is 29 files with 810 insertions; d18205d is 2 files against 32. Here `git diff mb..merged` contains other PRs' changes. The six most recent squashes were rebased first (merge-base equals the squash's parent), so the bug shows only when work runs in parallel, which the ship plan allows.
(b) In a scratch repo I modelled release/drain as SHIP-PLAN L66-68 defines it: P1's squash plus cherry-picks of P2b-2 and P3a. On a fix branch cut from it, `git diff main...HEAD` listed the fix, p2b.py and p3a_migration.py, so the cherry-picked phases fire on every drain-tool fix. Against `release/drain...HEAD` only the fix appears.
(c) Run on main, the diff is empty, which prints the vacuous one line.
(d) With unrelated history the command fails: `fatal: main...HEAD: no merge base`, exit 128.
(e) Main holds 135 merge commits. In the KS-5 replay `--diff <parent>` is ambiguous for them, and `--diff` has no head argument, so a replay or reviewer must check out each SHA.
attacks.consequence:
§7.2 and §5.2 need four changes:
- Base: `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` after fetch for branches from main; the release branch itself for branches from release/drain or release/drain-web.
- `ks close` uses `<merged>^1..<merged>`, the first parent.
- An empty range or a missing merge base exits with a distinct code, never a miss.
- The KS-5 replay uses first parents, counted per PR.
Add `--head <sha>` and `--repo <path>` to `ks lookup` (§7.1), and have the header print the base and head SHAs it used.

attacks.attack: 7. Worktrees on old branches running an old tools/ks CLI against a newer store schema (§9 version skew): what does the --diff join do, and does the phase go on silently?
attacks.evidence:
Text-level gap only; nothing runnable exists.
- Design:525 specifies that an old CLI rebuilds its own index and refuses to write events of a newer schema. It says nothing about reads. A `--diff` lookup writes only to the host-local log, so an old CLI answers from an old fold, and what it does with unknown event kinds or item types (symbol_span after KS-6b, guarded_refs) is unspecified.
- The critic offered a single pinned CLI in the store home (refute/critic.md, 'fix' option a); the design took option b, which covers writes only.
- release/drain is 'P1's squash commit' plus cherry-picks only (SHIP-PLAN L66-68). It therefore has no tools/ks unless KS-1 merged before P1, and §7.6 then says the phase 'proceeds without it'.
attacks.consequence: Either run ks from one copy pinned to origin/main in the store home, or have a lookup by a CLI older than the newest event schema in the journal exit with a distinct `cli_outdated` code that the routine reports as 'diff check not run'. Extend KS-1's two-worktree version-skew test to lookups. What would settle it: that test, with an old CLI reading a journal that holds newer-schema events.

attacks.attack: 8. The first-commit run when the first commit is the whole change (one-PR phases such as P12a): is 'an early hint' honest, and does the PR-ready run add anything?
attacks.evidence: Design:446 already says it is 'an early hint, not a pre-edit guard: in a one-PR phase the first commit can be the whole change', and P12a is 'one small PR' (SHIP-PLAN L656-664). In history, 106 of 133 merge PRs were single-commit, and four of seven recent squash branches had one commit (fix/identity-lockout, completion-replay, unauthenticated-availability, whatsapp-consent-optin). In most phases, then, the first-commit and PR-ready runs see the same diff, and any warning arrives after the code is written.
attacks.consequence: The wording is honest. Make the PR-ready run print 'same head as the first-commit run, not re-run' when HEAD has not moved, so a duplicate turn is not counted as a second check. Do not claim pre-edit value for it.

attacks.attack: 9. Cost per run, three runs per code phase: the join itself, and the token cost of its output under the 2,000-character cap. Does 'one line when nothing is protected' hold?
attacks.evidence:
one.mjs runs a full simulation in a fresh node process: merge-base, `git diff --name-only`, `git diff -U0`, tokenising, and a node:sqlite join against 80 seed items. Medians over 11 runs:
- #169 (7 files, +329): 197 ms
- #170 (22 files, +2003, 15.8k hunk tokens): 204 ms
- #173 (2 files): 207 ms
Of that, node start is 51 ms, git 120-190 ms and the join 2-14 ms. The real CLI's freshness check (23-35 ms at 5k events, KS-C4) is not included.
Output: 86 characters (about 89 tokens at 0.4 per character plus 55) with no warning; 460-650 characters (about 240-315 tokens) with a warning card and a '+N more' line.
The one-line case holds for the diff part. With `--action` in the same call it holds only if the action match also misses, which needs the store to test.
attacks.consequence: Cost is not an objection: about 0.6 s of compute per phase, dominated by turns (§7.7). Reword §7.6 to 'one line when neither the diff nor the action matches'.

attacks.attack: 10. Can the Opus reviewer's §7.6 sentence ('runs ks lookup --diff at the PR head SHA and names every do-not-apply warning') be satisfied vacuously, and what makes it checkable?
attacks.evidence:
Five routes to a vacuous pass:
- §7.1:431 says exits 3 (unavailable) and 4 (busy) are what 'callers treat as a miss', and the Routing sentence (design:469) has no exit-code clause. A reviewer following the text reports 'no warnings'.
- The CLI has no head argument, so a reviewer not checked out at the PR head diffs the wrong HEAD.
- The base is unspecified (attack 6). The empty case is shown in the scratch repo.
- A worktree that predates tools/ks has no CLI.
- The one-card rule limits 'every warning it printed' to at most one (attack 11).
Nothing checks the reviewer ran it. Lookups go to the host-local log, but `ks close` does not check for one at the final head.
attacks.consequence: Rewrite the Routing sentence: the reviewer runs the current CLI with `--diff <base> --head <PR head SHA>` and quotes the header line verbatim (base, head, journal watermark, counts per kind, warnings, exit code). Exit 3 or 4, a missing CLI, or a base or head mismatch is stated as 'diff check not run', never as 'no warnings'. `ks close` reports whether a `--diff` lookup at the PR's final head SHA exists in the host-local log.

attacks.attack: 11 (added). The one-card cap: can a do-not-apply warning be hidden when several entries match?
attacks.evidence: Simulating #170 (da988e2) with the realistic seed, 12 entries matched, among them ex3 (open_defect) and ex4 and ex6 (do_not_apply). One card fits, and it went to ex1a, which matched through CLAUDE.md prose. The ordering among warnings is undefined: §3.7 says only ORDER BY …, entry_id. The text is also inconsistent: §4.1:303 has 'any do-not-apply warning lines' inside the cap, while §7.1:431 and §7.2:446 say 'at most one warning card'.
attacks.consequence: Print one line per warning (entry id, kind, matched token, path:line), ordered do_not_apply, then open_defect, then trap, all inside the 2,000-character cap (12 lines is about 1,450 characters), plus at most one full card for the first. Reconcile §4.1, §7.1 and §7.2.

attacks.attack: 12 (added). Docs and prose hunks: do changes to .md files fire warnings?
attacks.evidence: Docs-only PRs fired through prose that names the identifiers: 906b990 (HANDOFF) fired ex3, ex4 and ex6; 5acd4cc (restore runbook) fired ex4; 7006d5a (phase-0 audit) fired ex3 and ex4. Across the replay, U0all against U0code was 93 against 81 PRs. The rule does not exclude docs, and this design document names every worked-example handle.
attacks.consequence: In §7.1, match docs hunks (*.md, docs/) separately and report them as one counted line, never a warning card. HANDOFF-style prescriptions already have their own route (`--prescription` / `doc_ref`).

attacks.attack: 13 (added). Context width and line sign are unspecified: -U0 against -U3, and + only against + and −.
attacks.consequence: In §7.1 and the KS-2 done-when, specify -U0 with --no-color, --no-ext-diff, --no-textconv and --no-renames, and tokens from both + and − lines.

attacks.attack: 14 (added). Are the KS-5 synthetic forbidden diffs self-fulfilling?
attacks.evidence: Every synthetic diff in KS-5 (design:614) is written by someone who knows the handles. A test-only inversion of ex6's protective assertion (test_identity_integration.py:103, `assert locked.status_code == 429, locked.text`) yields the tokens {assert, locked, status_code, text}. None of them is an ex6 handle, so under the rule as written it is path_only and prints nothing. Likewise a pure rename of the protective test has zero hunks, and a second-door new file in the working tree is invisible (attack 5).
attacks.consequence: Add adversarial forbidden diffs to KS-5's diff arm, written by a session that has not seen the handles: a test-only inversion, a second-door file (committed and untracked), a rename of the protective test, and a deletion-only removal of the age guard. Report per-handle historic fire rates and the share of fires that come only through whole-file preconditions.

counter_evidence:
Each of these is a measurement or demonstration on this box against this repository's history (first-parent, 154 PRs) or a scratch copy:
- **Path overlap still prints.** ex3's whole-file JobDetail.jsx precondition fires on 11 of 154 PRs with no ex3 token in the hunks. §4.1:301 also makes a changed path an exact ident hit, because files are ident handles (design:260).
- **Nothing bounds common identifiers.** Under the rule as written, a realistic 15-entry seed fires on 103 of 154 PRs, against 85 for a path-only join. Common identifiers fire on 17-66% of PRs (useState 31%, client_id 22%).
- **A do-not-apply warning can be hidden.** With one card printed, a multi-hit PR such as #170 (12 entries matched) can hide ex4 and ex6 behind a trap matched through CLAUDE.md.
- **Working-tree runs are blind to new files.** `git diff <base>` and `git stash create` cannot see an untracked second-door file; `stash create` returns nothing.
- **The `ks close` range pulls in other PRs.** 'Merge-base to the squash commit' includes other PRs in 59 of 133 historical merges (ef8ae86: 1 file of its own against 29 in the range).
- **Drain branches inherit other phases.** A release/drain branch diffed against main's merge-base includes the cherry-picked phases.
- **The reviewer step can pass vacuously.** Exit 3 or 4 is defined as a miss, so the reviewer sentence can be satisfied without the check having run.
trace:
What holds, with evidence:
- **It sees every committed edit, with no hook.** git diff reads the tree, so Bash, PowerShell and subagent edits are all seen once committed. The CRLF+BOM rewrite was normalised to a one-line change.
- **Function grain is reachable with curated handles.** Matching curated, rare identifiers on -U0 lines gives grain close to function level on shared files. AppContext.jsx: 3 of 13 PRs fire with {logPayment, logPaymentApi, PaymentModal}, reproducing the design's 13/3 figure. ex4's handles fire on 6 of the 39 PRs that touch its files.
- **The pilot pair can be met.** The naive ex3 fix fires (randomUUID, clientId) while unrelated AppContext.jsx edits stay silent under -U0.
- **Committed runs see new files.** A committed second-door file shows fully in `git diff <base>...HEAD`.
- **It is cheap.** About 200 ms a run, and the output is far under the 2,000-character cap.
narrowed_claim:
`ks lookup --diff` is a hook-free check over committed ranges. It sees every committed edit however it was made, and costs about 0.2 s plus one agent turn per run. It prints a do_not_apply, open_defect or trap warning before merge, and gets function-like grain on shared files, when six conditions hold:
1. Tokens come from both + and − lines of a -U0 diff of code files.
2. Ident handles are curated, high-specificity identifiers whose historic fire rate is bounded at write time.
3. File-kind idents and whole-file preconditions count as path_only.
4. Docs hunks are counted separately.
5. Every warning gets one line, do_not_apply first.
6. The base is the branch's own first-parent base: the release branch for drain worktrees, `<merged>^1` for `ks close`.

It does not see untracked files in working-tree mode unless the temporary-index snapshot is used. It does not see ignored files or out-of-repo operator actions. Before KS-6b it has no span clause, so the pilot measures the token rule and the config-value rule only.
what_would_settle_it:
Things that remain unverifiable need the store or a decision:
- Old-CLI read behaviour on newer-schema events: settled by the KS-1 two-worktree version-skew test extended to `ks lookup --diff`.
- Whether `--action` in the same call keeps the quiet case to one line: settled by the KS-2 fixture tests with seeded action handles.
- The real false-fire rate: settled by the actual KS-4 ident handles, which do not exist yet, replayed with replay.mjs's method (first-parent, -U0, both signs, code-only).

amendments.change: Define the hunk-level rule exactly. Range: `git diff -U0 --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames <base> <head>`. Tokens: word tokens from both + and − lines, with strings and comments kept (SQL inside op.execute, env names). A warning needs a symbol, env-name or error-code ident among those tokens, or a config-key value change. File-kind ident handles, renames, and preconditions or protective-test items held as whole-file blobs are path_only (logged, not printed) until KS-6b builds spans. Docs hunks (*.md, docs/) are reported as one counted line, never a card. Add `--head <sha>` and `--repo <path>`. The header line prints the base and head SHAs, the journal watermark, counts per kind, the number of warnings and path_only items, and the exit code.
amendments.why: Before KS-6b the span clause is empty. A whole-file precondition (JobDetail.jsx) fires on 11 of 154 PRs. §4.1:301 makes a changed path an ident hit. -U3 against -U0 and the line sign change the result (scratch repo). Docs PRs fire through prose.

amendments.change: Replace it with: one line per warning (entry id, kind, matched token, path:line), ordered do_not_apply, then open_defect, then trap, then entry_id, all inside the 2,000-character cap; plus at most one full card, for the first.
amendments.why: In #170, 12 entries matched and the one card went to a trap matched in CLAUDE.md, hiding ex4 and ex6. §4.1:303 and §7.1:431/§7.2:446 contradict each other.

amendments.change: Every ident handle a do_not_apply, open_defect or trap entry uses for `--diff` is replayed against the -U0 changed code lines of origin/main's first-parent history. A handle above the agreed share of PRs is refused or tightened, and `ks record` prints each handle's historic count. Handles for a do_not_apply entry are named guarded identifiers, never derived from the fix diff.
amendments.why: Exact ident hits carry no IDF. useState is in 31% of PRs, client_id 22%, payload 17%, randomUUID and clientId 8% each. Handles derived from the ex3 fix diff fire every unrelated variant.

amendments.change: Define the base: `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` after fetch for branches from main; release/drain or release/drain-web for branches cut from them. `ks close` diffs `<merged>^1..<merged>`, never 'merge-base to the squash commit'. An empty range or a missing merge base exits with a distinct code reported as 'diff check not run'.
amendments.why: In 59 of 133 historical merges the branch was behind main (ef8ae86: 1 file of its own against 29 in the range). A drain-branch diff against main's merge-base includes the cherry-picked P2b-2 and P3a. On main the range is empty; with unrelated history git exits 128.

amendments.change: Working-tree runs include untracked, non-ignored files: a temporary index outside the repository (GIT_INDEX_FILE, `read-tree HEAD`, `add -N` for `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`), which writes no objects. Failing that, return inconclusive(untracked_present) whenever any such file exists. Never fall back to HEAD when `git stash create` returns nothing.
amendments.why: A new untracked second-door file is invisible to `git diff <base>` and to `git stash create`, which returns an empty string. The KS-F19 guard cannot match a new path. The temporary-index method made the file visible with 23 objects before and after.

amendments.change: Replace it with: 'The reviewer runs the current `ks lookup --diff <base> --head <PR head SHA>`, quotes its header line verbatim, and names every do-not-apply warning line and how the diff respects it; exit 3 or 4, a missing CLI or a base/head mismatch is reported as "diff check not run", never as no warnings.' `ks close` reports whether a `--diff` lookup at the PR's final head SHA exists in the host-local log. In §7.1, exits 3 and 4 are a miss for retrieval only, never for `--diff`.

amendments.change: Replay per PR over first-parent commits, with `<parent>` = `^1`. Add adversarial forbidden diffs written by a session that has not seen the handles: a test-only inversion of test_identity_integration.py:103, a second-door file (committed and untracked), a pure rename of a protective test, and a deletion-only removal of `_MAX_DISPATCH_EVENT_AGE`. Or adopt the critic's option (a), one CLI pinned to origin/main in the store home. Note that release/drain worktrees carry no tools/ks unless KS-1 precedes P1.

amendments.section: §12.7 'What was not applied, and one interpretation'
amendments.change: Add: the AppContext.jsx pair is satisfiable only with -U0, both line signs and curated handles; the naive PaymentModal fix fires through randomUUID and clientId or through the JobDetail.jsx whole-file precondition, not through logPayment; the whole-file precondition makes every JobDetail.jsx edit fire until KS-6b.

amendments.section: §7.6 phase-routine text ('one line when nothing in the store touches the change') and §7.2

changes_a_127_ruling:
Amends KS-O10, KS-O11, KS-O14 and the §12.7 'one interpretation' paragraph; reverses nothing.
- **KS-O10:** the hunk-level rule needs an exact definition. File-kind idents and whole-file preconditions become path_only before KS-6b. There is one line per warning, do_not_apply first. `ks close` uses the merged commit's first parent instead of 'merge-base to the squash commit'. Base rules cover release/drain.
- **KS-O11:** the reviewer quotes the header, and exits 3 or 4 or a missing CLI count as 'not run'.
- **KS-O14:** the replay uses first parents, adds adversarial forbidden diffs and reports per-handle fire rates.
